newsitem.title: CHINA: China adds five billion yuan new share issue quota.
newsitem.headline: China adds five billion yuan new share issue quota.

text.p: China's securities authorities have announced an extra five billion yuan on the 1996 quota of new share issues for issue this year or after, the Shanghai Securities News reported on Monday.

The newspaper quoted a spokesman for the China Securities Regulatory Commission as saying the original 1996 share issue quota set in Decemnber last year was 15 billion yuan, but at the time only 10 billion yuan was made public.
He said the focus for share issues this year was medium and large-scale state-owned enterprises whose share requirements were large.
As a result the originally-announced level of 10 billion yuan had proved to be insufficient.
Analysts said the announcement would result in a faster pace of new share issues and listings, which would have the effect of cooling down China's stock markets.
The exchanges in Shanghai and Shenzhen have risen sharply in recently months in spite of continuous warnings on risk and overheating from Beijing's securities authorities.
The share quota announced in December was already almost twice as big as the 5.5 billion yuan quota announced a year previously.
The share issue quota is released at the end of each year basically for use in the following 12 months. But if unused, quota can be carried over to the next year, depending on market conditions.
